autonomyAvailability.why: post-fix (2026-11-22T02:00:00Z → 2026-11-22T18:03:49Z): 64/64 scheduled slots good (0 missing), Wilson low 0.9434 ⇒ the volume supports NO candidate yet; earliest support if every future slot is good: 97% ≈ 2026-11-23T09:18:49.000Z, 98% ≈ 2026-11-24T01:18:49.000Z, 99% ≈ 2026-11-26T01:18:49.000Z. Residual (non-organizational) unavailability 2026-11-08T00:00:00Z → asOf = 5/1414 slots (0.35%: legitimate 1, integrity 0, unclassified 0, missing ticks 4), Wilson of good [0.9917, 0.9985]. That COUNTERFACTUAL estimate (organizational refusals removed, not observed post-fix) would sit at the edge of 99%, but it is not a measurement of the post-fix regime. 98% is kept PROVISIONAL (not raised to 99%) because (a) only the post-fix window is measured and it supports nothing yet, (b) the scheduled-slot SLI now also charges timer/host outages: the 14-day budget is ≈26.88 slots at 98% vs ≈13.44 at 99% — a single ~4 h host/timer outage (16 slots) would exhaust 99% but not 98%. Upgrade path (PROPOSED): move to 99% only if, after ≥ 14 post-fix days, the measured scheduled-slot Wilson low is ≥ 0.99.
autonomyAvailability.evaluateOn: mission-attempt-log from 2026-11-22T02:00:00Z; unavailable = STARTUP_REFUSED | AUDIT_CHAIN_TAMPERED | any status outside the producer allowlist | missing scheduled slot (gap > 1.5 × 15 min)

ciMainPush.why: SLI 0.9956 = 450/452 decisive push-to-main runs, window 2026-11-08T22:11:44Z → 2026-11-22T04:58:16Z (13.28 days, static snapshot docs/odg/evidence/LOT3_CI_EVENTS.json fetched 2026-11-22 with gh run list -L 1000 — NOT a rolling 30-day window), Wilson 95% [0.984, 0.9988]. 97%: SUPPORTED, budget left 0.8525; 98%: SUPPORTED, budget left 0.7788; 98.5%: INCONCLUSIVE, budget left 0.705; 99%: INCONCLUSIVE, budget left 0.5575. Rule: tightest candidate inside the interval with budget not exhausted ⇒ 0.99. The previous 98% came from mixing 530 pull_request runs (14 failures = the check catching bad PR code) into the SLI; on main-push alone 98% is already met with margin (too loose to detect a degradation). At ~34.04 main pushes/day a 30-day 99% budget is ≈10.21 failures. 99% is a target, NOT a claim that it is met (it is inside the interval, i.e. unproven).

missionReliability.why: only 3 mission attempt(s) reached by a tick (pass 1, fail 0, policy-refused 2) — below minSampleN 20; no rate reported. Policy refusals stay not-pass in the SLI (fail-closed) but are shown separately: they are canary authorization denials, not execution failures.

alerts.rule: alert if ≥ 4 consecutive unavailable scheduled slots (1 h, missing ticks included) OR ≥ 4 unavailable slots in one UTC day (burn ≥ 2× at 98%: 2 × 0.02 × 96 = 3.84)
alert on every failed push-to-main run (at ~34.04 runs/day one failure already burns > 2× the daily 99% budget, so a per-day burn alert degenerates to 'any failure')

freezeRules.rule: if the rolling 14-day budget is exhausted: no change to mission-runner / Truth-Lock / scheduler code other than availability fixes, until the budget is positive again
if the rolling 30-day budget is exhausted: merges to main restricted to CI/reliability fixes until the budget is positive again
